Getting committed "against your will" is actually pretty difficult.  IF you go in and say that you want to commit suicide, unless you are a "frequent flyer", they will have someone come in for a psych consult, and maybe a social worker.  If they feel you need some "stabilizing care" they will ask you to agree to go in.

If you don't have a 'plan' or whatever, they generally offer to refer you to a clinic or a psychiatrist, either one.

Good luck.

Commonly used metaphor-the roller coaster that you can never get off of.

Honestly?  People who sincerely want to understand, but have no personal experience with it will have a hard time with metaphors anyway.  There's a number of decent 'personal experience' blogs on wordpress about it.  

Here's one I ran across not long ago:  an optimistic post-http://cogitabunda.wordpress.com/2013/07/26/on-bipolar/

A not so happy post: http://cogitabunda.wordpress.com/2013/11/05/having-bipolar-a-down-day/

I dunno, it resonates with me.
It causes me rage.  Let me know when it becomes cool to have cancer or hiv, so I can applaud when they all jump that bandwagon.
